post.caption: The Lone Ranger's ring held polonium. In 1947, Kix cereal offered a Lone Ranger Atomic Bomb Ring for 15 cents and a box top. Its red tail fin hid a speck of polonium facing a tiny screen. In a dark room, a lens showed flashes of light, each one a particle hitting the screen. The ads called the ring perfectly safe and promised atoms splitting to smithereens. The polonium fades by half every 138 days, so surviving rings no longer glow.
